text:
olivia: Heads-up: user on Windows 3.9 hit weird behavior in our async sample. Root error is CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED but our async client surfaces it as a generic ConnectionError with no cert hint. Sync sample clearly shows the SSL error.
dan: That's bad for debugging. Async httpx stack can wrap SSL failures; retries make it worse if a retry swallows the original exception. Do we attach the original exception to the retry?
kevin: We currently retry on transient network errors but our retry middleware re-raises a new RequestError without the original __cause__. We should preserve the chain so users see the SSLCertVerificationError.
sara: Also, typing mismatch: sync client accepts `verify` and respects REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE; async accepts `ssl` context in code, but our stubs only document `verify: bool` and don't expose `ssl` in the AsyncClient signature. Mypy users are confused and try `verify=certifi.where()` which fails.
olivia: The repro on Windows: python 3.9.12, python.org installer, certifi installed, async sample `await AsyncClient.generate(...)` -> ConnectionError. When I run with logging I can see inner SSLCertVerificationError.
dan: Short-term fix: update retry logic to chain exceptions and add clearer logging that surfaces SSL verification failures. Long-term: make async and sync APIs align (accept both `verify` and `ssl`), and document Windows-specific note about SSL_CERT_FILE/certifi.where().
kevin: I'll open a tiny patch: 1) preserve __cause__ when re-raising in retry middleware, 2) add Optional[ssl.SSLContext] to AsyncClient type stub, 3) add a one-liner in the Windows onboarding sample showing how to create ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where()).
sara: Also request: add a CI job that runs the async tests on Windows with py3.9 and py3.11 to catch regressions.
devex-bot: created issue 2510: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/issues/2510 - "windows-async-ssl-exception-chaining-typing-ci"
olivia: thanks, that should make error messages much more actionable for customers. :thumbsup:
